title: Midway as a wargame
label: A wargame played with the real forces. The record is on the other side of the table.

arena.note: Open sea, some 5,000 m deep: the midpoint of the two carrier forces at 05:52, when the Catalina's report of carriers steaming south-east is the first contact in the box, 350 km apart in the record and 5 km in the arena, on the bearing between them then (the Kidō Butai 252° from TF 16 and TF 17, the box's tracks).

japan.name: The Kidō Butai
japan.leader: Vice Admiral NAGUMO Chūichi 南雲忠一

formation.note: The four carriers in a box 6 to 9 km on a side in the record (R4 §3.2; the box's stations round Akagi), drawn in as a circle round the guide 1,600 m across, with the battleships, cruisers and destroyers on the screen ring; all on 135°, as Akagi steams at 07:00 in the box.

aircraft.note: the morning combat air patrol (the box's cap-morning)
the Midway strike's escort (strike-akagi-a6m)
the Midway strike's dive bombers (strike-akagi-d3a), armed against ships in the arena
the patrol that met Torpedo Eight (cap-vt8)
strike-kaga-a6m
strike-kaga-d3a, armed against ships in the arena
strike-soryu-a6m
the Midway strike's level bombers (strike-soryu-b5n), with torpedoes in the arena
the patrol that met Torpedo Three, Hiryū's and the others' (cap-vt3)
the escorts of Hiryū's first and second strikes (hiryu-a6m-1, hiryu-a6m-2)
Hiryū's first strike, on Yorktown at 12:05 (hiryu-d3a-1)
Hiryū's second strike, on Yorktown at 14:44 (hiryu-b5n-2)

goal.text: Put two of the three American carriers out of action before 10:00.

phases.title: Break up the torpedo attacks
phases.text: American torpedo planes come in low and slow, one squadron after another: shoot down six of them.

phases.title: Dive bombers overhead
phases.text: Dive bombers are over the fleet while the fighters are down low: keep all four carriers afloat.

phases.title: Launch the counterstrike
phases.text: The counterstrike is away: get six aircraft through to within 1,500 m of an American carrier.

phases.title: Bombs on the carrier
phases.text: The dive bombers push over on the nearest carrier: put three bombs on her deck.

phases.title: The torpedo planes
phases.text: The torpedo planes split to come in on both bows: put two torpedoes into a carrier.

usa.name: TF 16 and TF 17
usa.leader: Rear Admirals Frank Jack Fletcher and Raymond A. Spruance

formation.note: TF 16 and TF 17 steamed apart in the record, each a carrier ring of cruisers and destroyers; the arena draws them as one circle round Enterprise, the carriers 1,600 m across and the screen on the ring; all on 135°, into the south-east wind to launch, as Enterprise steams at 07:00 in the box.

Torpedo Six (vt-6)
Fighting Six (vf-6)
TF 16's fighters sent to TF 17 at noon (tf16-cap-noon)
Bombing Eight, Scouting Eight and the group commander (hornet-sbd), who did not find the carriers in the record
Torpedo Eight (vt-8), the first to reach the carriers in the record
Fighting Eight (vf-8)
Bombing Three (vb-3)
Scouting Five, kept back for the searches in the record (vs-5-search)
Torpedo Three (vt-3)
Fighting Three's escort of Torpedo Three (vf-3-escort)
Yorktown's combat air patrols at noon and at 14:40 (vf-3-cap-noon, vf-3-cap-1430)

goal.text: Put three of the four Japanese carriers out of action before 10:00.

phases.title: The torpedo squadrons go in
phases.text: Hornet's, Enterprise's and Yorktown's torpedo planes come in low from different sides: put a torpedo into a carrier.

phases.title: The dive bombers arrive
phases.text: The Zeros are down low chasing the torpedo planes: push over and put three bombs on the carriers' decks.

phases.title: The counterstrike
phases.text: Japanese dive bombers and fighters are inbound on the carriers: shoot down six of them before they push over.

phases.title: Find the last carrier
phases.text: A Japanese carrier is still launching: put two bombs on her deck.

phases.title: Hold on
phases.text: Keep two of the three carriers afloat to the end.

footnote: On 4 June 1942 dive bombers from Enterprise and Yorktown set Kaga, Akagi and Sōryū ablaze between 10:22 and 10:26 and Hiryū at about 17:00, and all four were lost; Yorktown, hit by Hiryū's dive bombers and torpedo planes, was torpedoed by the submarine I-168 on 6 June and sank the next morning.
